Archaeological Sources
Ashokan Edictsand inscriptions:Thereare Rock Edicts, Pillar Edictsand
Cave Inscriptions located at several places in the Indian sub-continent:
Their importance came to be appreciated only after their decipheration
by James Princep in 1837 and also the identification of Ashoka as the
author of these edicts in the beginning of the 2Oth century Majority
of them are in the nature of Ashoka' s proclamations to the public at
large,and only a small group of them describe his own acceptance of
Buddhism and his relationship with the Sangha (Commune). Though
Prakritwas the language used in them, the script varied from region to
region Kharoshti in the North-West,  Greek and Aramaic in the West
and Brahmiin the East of India)
